title: CTE Teacher Certification/Endorsement in Maine
before:
NOTE: All decisions regarding Teacher Certification/Endorsement within the State of Maine are handled through the Maine Certification Team.

Individuals wishing to become CTE teachers have a number of paths they can follow to reach that goal. Below are resources to assist in that process.

  • CTE Endorsement Requirements
  • Chapter 115 provides a brief outline of the five different pathways that one may follow to become a CTE instructor. Choose "Part II" and jump to page 44.
  • Certification Team: This link goes directly to the DOE Certification Office web page.
  • Courses available at EMCC: This is one of the places where CTE teacher certification courses are provided.
  • NOCTI: To request a NOCTI instructor assessment for certification purposes, complete the NOCTI Assessment Request Form and submit to Danielle Despins-Kelley at danielle.r.despins@maine.gov.

decisions.label: Write the email addresses the same way
decisions.why: 1 address is shown in whatever case it was typed in. The house form capitalises each name and leaves a middle initial in lower case — danielle.r.despins@maine.gov → Danielle.r.Despins@maine.gov. Only the first letter of each part changes, so a name that spells itself LaBreck keeps doing so.

decisions.label: Tag a document link with the format it opens
decisions.why: 1 link on this page opens a file — 1 Excel — and says nothing about it, while others in the same list carry a tag because their author typed one. The format is read from the file name, so the list stops being half-labelled. No link text changes.

decisions.label: Separate a link from its description
decisions.why: 4 list items open with a link and then explain it, all at the same weight — so the thing you can click is no easier to find than the sentence about it. The link becomes the item and the explanation sits under it.

decisions.label: Let a colon do its own work
decisions.why: A colon marks the words before it as a term and the words after it as what the term means. 2 links sit immediately in front of a colon, where the chevron lands between the term and the punctuation that belongs to it. No word changes and nothing is removed.

decisions.label: Make a loose address look like an address
decisions.why: 1 email address sits in the body of this page rather than in a contact block, drawn exactly like every other link — so the one that opens a mail window looks the same as the ones that go to web pages. The chip carries the same envelope the banner's contact link uses. The address itself does not change.

decisions.label: Use this paragraph as the page description
decisions.why: It is the page’s own opening paragraph, moved into the banner rather than rewritten.
decisions.value: Individuals wishing to become CTE teachers have a number of paths they can follow to reach that goal. Below are resources to assist in that process.

decisions.label: Start a description with a capital
decisions.why: 1 description begins with a small letter, because it used to run on from the link after a dash. The dash is gone and the link now sits above in its own face, so each description opens a line of its own. One character changes and only ever the first.
